html:
The last complete symphony of Ludwig van Beethoven, first performed in Vienna on 7 May 1824. It is famous for its final movement, in which singers join the orchestra to sing the Ode to Joy.

Using voices in a symphony was new. The words come from a poem by Friedrich Schiller about joy and the brotherhood of all people. The symphony is long and builds over four movements toward this hymn.

Beethoven was by then almost completely deaf. He stood on stage at the premiere beside the conductor, and the story goes that at the end one of the singers turned him around so he could see the crowd cheering, which he could not hear.

The work became one of the most performed and admired in Western music, a model for later composers such as Brahms and Wagner. The Council of Europe adopted the Ode to Joy melody as its anthem in 1972, and the European Union later took it as the anthem of Europe.
